name: The Crownlands

find the man who was seen leaving the garrison at midnight
learn who holds the deed to the old estate

find the man who left the garrison at midnight (2)
learn who holds the true deed to the estate (3)
prevent the youngest heir from signing the division (4)
carry word of the exiled lord's survival to a trusted ear (5)
track the missing twin from the harbor to wherever they fled (6)

regions.name: The Regency Seat
regions.description: The court and garrison of the acting regent — cold, formal, watchful.

regions.name: The Divided Estate
regions.description: A great house split between rival heirs, its east wing locked, its staff diminished.

regions.name: The Merchant Quarter
regions.description: Harbor docks and counting houses where the Merchant League moves letters and people.

regions.name: The Crossroads
regions.description: Where three roads meet and three old women are sometimes found. Not always the same ones.

factions.name: The Regency
factions.description: The court council holding power in the absence of a clear heir. Legitimate by paperwork, not blood.
factions.agenda: Maintain control until succession is settled. Suppress any claimant who would upset the balance.

factions.name: The Wandering Faithful
factions.description: A scattered order of monks who move their chapel quarterly. They keep records no one else keeps.
factions.agenda: Preserve history, provide sanctuary, watch. They know where the exiled go.

factions.name: The Merchant League
factions.description: Counting-house families who backed the wrong succession once and are quietly backing a different one now.
factions.agenda: A stable ruler who will honor their old trade agreements. They are not particular about which one.

npcs.name: Aldric
npcs.archetype: exiled lord living as a woodcutter who will not say his name
npcs.hook: Has lived under a false name for four years. Knows the estate's east wing key is inside the garrison chapel. Will not act unless someone shows him the letter.

npcs.name: Ensign Breck
npcs.archetype: garrison lieutenant corroded by unearned suspicion
npcs.hook: Believes someone in the garrison is passing letters to the exiled lord. He is not wrong, but he suspects the wrong person.

npcs.name: Maret
npcs.archetype: courier traveling in disguise on a mission she cannot explain
npcs.hook: Carries a letter she has not read and was told not to. Has been recognized once already. Needs a place to wait out the night.

npcs.name: Calder
npcs.archetype: young man paralyzed by grief for a father he barely knew
npcs.hook: The eldest heir. His father died in the garrison infirmary three weeks ago. He arrived at the estate to find it already divided by his younger siblings.

npcs.name: Wynne
npcs.archetype: apothecary who measures truth in what she does not say
npcs.hook: Prepared the draught that the garrison infirmary ordered the night of the old lord's death. Has said nothing. Will say nothing unless given a reason to believe silence is more dangerous.

npcs.name: Sevin
npcs.archetype: surviving twin carrying the wrong name and the right guilt
npcs.hook: Was declared drowned. Has been living as their twin's identity for seven months. The twin is alive too, somewhere in the harbor district.

npcs.name: Lord Harevast
npcs.archetype: old lord who gave everything away and now has nothing to ask
npcs.hook: Divided the estate among three children while still living, expecting gratitude. Has been given a small room near the kitchen. No longer receives visitors by default.

npcs.name: The Three at the Crossroads
npcs.archetype: three crones at a crossroads who finish each other's sentences
npcs.hook: Always found at the crossroads between midnight and dawn. Speak in thirds — one begins, another continues, the third ends. They know about the exiled lord, the letter, and the twin. They will not be asked twice.

threads.name: The Deposed
threads.description: A lord was removed from power on thin charges four years ago. He is alive, nearby, and not yet ready to act. The Regency knows he exists but not where he sleeps.

threads.name: The General's Marriage
threads.description: A senior officer's trust in his household has been methodically destroyed by someone with nothing to gain from it except watching. The damage is not yet visible but will be soon.

threads.name: The Divided Estate
threads.description: An old lord split his estate three ways while still living. Two heirs have already moved to consolidate against the third. The old lord is still there, in the kitchen room, watching.

threads.name: The Drowned Twin
threads.description: One twin was declared dead at sea seven months ago. The survivor took their name and their prospects. The drowned twin is alive and has recently arrived at the harbor, asking questions.

threads.name: The Three at the Crossroads
threads.description: Three old women appear at the crossroads between midnight and dawn and speak futures to anyone who stops. Everything they have said so far has come true. The Regency wants them moved on. No one has managed it.

seeds.hint: The letter in the garrison fire was unsigned. The handwriting matches the regent's secretary.
Aldric knows where the east wing key is hidden. He left it there himself, the night he was removed.
The suspicion consuming Breck was put there deliberately. Someone wanted him distracted.
The letter Maret carries is a confession, not a message. The person who wrote it is now dead.
A second will exists. The youngest heir knows where it is. They will not produce it voluntarily.
Wynne prepared a sleeping draught, not a poison. But she does not know that what she prepared was altered before it was used.
Sevin and their twin have been using each other's names since childhood. Not all of their debts are their own.
Lord Harevast divided the estate to prevent war. He believed they would still include him. He was wrong about both things.
The Three at the Crossroads have spoken seven futures so far. All seven have come to pass. The eighth is still unspoken.
The Regency is not neutral on succession. One council member has a daughter. The paperwork is already drafted.
The Merchant League backed Aldric's father. They have never publicly repudiated him. This is on purpose.
The Wandering Faithful have records of every exile the Regency has issued. They keep two copies.
Someone has been living in the east wing for at least three weeks. The food is going somewhere.
The garrison chapel has a grave that postdates the chapel's founding by thirty years. No name on the stone.
The Three have been found at the crossroads for over a hundred years. No one who has asked their age has received the same answer twice.
